mcp_surface_exists.evidence: POST /ai-gateway/mcp-services/<name> -> HTTP 403 and 200, both carrying a JSON-RPC envelope. An MCP dispatcher answered. Note the malformed-name probe returns HTTP 200 while its JSON-RPC body is an ERROR -- reading the status alone would score it a success, so any gateway health check on this route that asserts on status code will report a broken MCP service as healthy. That is worth a line in v1.6 on its own.
mcp_surface_exists.base_path_is_not_the_probe: GET /ai-gateway/mcp-services (no name, redirects NOT followed) -> 307. An earlier ad-hoc probe of this same URL reported 200 with a JSON-RPC body, and the difference was urllib following the 307 by default -- so the 200 belonged to a DIFFERENT URL than the one named in the result. Recorded because it is this repository's recurring defect in miniature: the measurement was real, the label was wrong, and nothing in the output said so.
mcp_surface_exists.contrast_with_m3: The legacy path /api/2.0/mcp/servers returns 404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND -- a different path with a different answer. M3's 404 was never evidence about M2.

path_shape_correction.server_requires: INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE: name must be of the form `mcp-services/{catalog}.{schema}.{leaf}`
path_shape_correction.why_it_matters: The segment is a three-part Unity Catalog name, not an opaque service slug. So M2's authorization scope is per-UC-OBJECT. Two consequences for v1.6: the route table's description of this path is wrong and should be corrected; and a gateway selector over this path is selecting over UC object names, which means the allow-list question for M2 is 'which catalog.schema.leaf may be invoked', not 'which service'. Those are different allow-lists with different owners.
path_shape_correction.base_path_307: POST /ai-gateway/mcp-services with no name -> 307. A reader probing the base path first sees a redirect and may conclude the route needs redirect handling. It does not; it needs a name.

post.jsonrpc_error_message: Not authorized to invoke MCP service.
post.reading: POST routes. The -32007 'Not authorized to invoke MCP service' is the dispatcher refusing on AUTHORIZATION after authenticating and routing -- which is what confirms the path and verb. It is NOT M2 being unreachable.

methods.conclusion: POST only. GET returns 405 on a well-formed name BOTH with and without text/event-stream in Accept, so the 405 is not content negotiation -- there is no GET event stream on this tier. route-table.yaml's `methods: [POST]` is correct and `methods_unconfirmed` can be cleared.

what_this_does_not_prove.invocation: No MCP tool was invoked. The dispatcher refused on authorization (-32007) because no MCP service is registered and entitled to this principal on this tier. So M2's END TO END behaviour -- a governed tool call through Gravitee to a Unity Gateway MCP service -- remains unexercised. What is settled is the route's method and path shape, which is what the selector needs and what OD-8's second half asked.
what_this_does_not_prove.the_stream_in_general: 'No GET stream on this tier' is not 'no GET stream'. A workspace with a registered MCP service may well offer one, and the MCP streamable-HTTP spec permits it. So the selector for a PRODUCTION M2 should still be reviewed against the tier it will run on. What this run removes is the need to GUESS: the question now has a method, and the method is 'probe GET on a well-formed name twice'.
what_this_does_not_prove.tool_restriction: M2 carries `tool_restriction: read-only tools only`. Nothing here tests that. It cannot be tested without an invocable service, and it is not a method question.
